issues.description: The UML in the problem statement specifies the Pneumatic interface with methods raisePressure(int) and openValve(), but the solution implementation of Pneumatic declares raisePressure(int) and releaseValve(). This name/signature mismatch between the specification and the provided solution is a structural inconsistency that can confuse students about which method to implement (openValve vs. releaseValve) and may cause automated checks or reference implementations to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Pneumatic interface consistent across all artifacts. Either (a) rename the method releaseValve() in src/de/tum/in/ase/Pneumatic.java (solution) to openValve(), matching the UML and task description, or (b) update the problem statement and tests to expect releaseValve() instead of openValve(). Ensure the template, solution, and problem statement all use the same method name/signature.

issues.description: The UML in the problem statement (interface Pneumatic) specifies a method named openValve(), and the solution's implementing classes (LaunchedDropdownTower, LaunchedRollerCoaster) implement openValve(), but the Pneumatic interface in the solution declares releaseValve() instead of openValve(). This inconsistent method name (openValve vs releaseValve) across problem statement and solution creates a mapping and compilation confusion for students.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Pneumatic interface method name with the UML and the implementing classes. Change the interface method releaseValve() to openValve(), or alternatively rename the implementations to override releaseValve(). Preferably update Pneumatic.java to declare openValve() to match the problem statement and existing implementing classes.
